I recently tried to deposit ₹50,000 into my US wallet, and the app showed an exchange rate of ₹96.25/USD, while the prevailing USD/INR rate at the time was around ₹94.26/USD. This represents a difference of approximately ₹1.99 per USD, or 2.1%, which is significant for a currency conversion. For a ₹50,000 transaction, this exchange-rate difference alone can materially reduce the USD amount received. The app also displayed ₹74.89 GST and ₹8,321 indicative TCS. I understand that TCS is refundable and therefore should not necessarily be considered a permanent cost. However, the exchange-rate spread is a separate issue and needs much greater transparency. My concern is not simply about paying a fee — it is about fair and transparent valuation of the money being converted. If Federal Bank/INDmoney is applying a currency-conversion markup, customers should clearly be shown the reference USD/INR rate, the markup/spread being applied, and the exact amount being charged because of that spread. The statement “You’re saving ₹1,796 on transfer charges and forex rates” also creates the impression that the conversion is highly competitive, while the displayed exchange rate appears materially higher than the prevailing market rate. I request INDmoney to clearly disclose how this exchange rate is determined and what portion of the difference represents the bank’s forex spread. Customers should be able to see a transparent calculation before approving the transaction. Please improve the transparency of USD/INR conversion rates and ensure customers receive a fair and properly evaluated exchange rate.
